description: Phase 0O.6F (ADR 0052 amendment; owner decision OWNER-0O6E-2026-09-26): the provider-neutral runtime security contract every production container of both images MUST be started with. It is a deployment REQUIREMENT, not a runtime default: no orchestrator is chosen, so each platform maps it to its own semantics (see provider_equivalents). Guarded by Tests\Feature\Configuration\RuntimeSecurityContractTest; proven by infrastructure/docker/production/verify-images.sh, which starts every container with reference_invocation.docker. A capability may be added back only by a later ADR.

required_verification_checks: app: hardened invocation -- not privileged, all capabilities dropped, none added, no-new-privileges
app: runs as www-data (uid 33) with no permitted, effective or bounding capability and NoNewPrivs=1
app: every process of the web, worker and scheduler roles is non-root with no capability and NoNewPrivs=1
app: mount/umount carry no setuid bit (dpkg-statoverride)
app: setuid/setgid execution gains no privilege under the hardened invocation
gateway: hardened invocation -- not privileged, all capabilities dropped, none added, no-new-privileges
gateway: runs as gateway (uid 10001) with no permitted, effective or bounding capability and NoNewPrivs=1
gateway: every process is non-root with no capability and NoNewPrivs=1
gateway: mount/umount carry no setuid bit (dpkg-statoverride)
gateway: setuid/setgid execution gains no privilege under the hardened invocation

provider_equivalents.docker / compose: never --privileged / privileged: true; --cap-drop ALL / cap_drop: [ALL]; no --cap-add / cap_add; --security-opt no-new-privileges:true
provider_equivalents.kubernetes: securityContext: privileged: false, allowPrivilegeEscalation: false, capabilities: {drop: [ALL]}, runAsNonRoot: true
provider_equivalents.other: the platform's documented equivalent of each contract field; an unsupported field blocks deployment

future_hardening.read_only_root_filesystem: NOT required in this checkpoint (0O.6F audit, docker diff of hardened containers). The application writes /tmp/nginx (pid and temp paths), /var/www/app/bootstrap/cache (config/route caches warmed at start) and /var/www/app/storage/framework/views (compiled views); the Gateway writes nothing. A plain --read-only root with EMPTY writable mounts over storage and bootstrap/cache fails at start (view:cache needs the storage/framework tree), so the future change must pre-create that tree (or warm the caches at build time) and mount only /tmp, storage and bootstrap/cache writable. The Gateway already runs with --read-only and a /tmp tmpfs.
